_README: Which companion-animal programmes already claim a target (amendment A15). Used to ANNOTATE
candidates, never to exclude them: a claimed target means the indication has a validated market.
Indexed three ways, because one was not enough. Raw target tokens alone matched junk - generic
words like 'inhibitor' and 'receptor' made sotagliflozin compete with Apoquel and inhaled
treprostinil compete with a pheromone diffuser - so those are stop-worded. Raw tokens alone also
matched nothing where it mattered: Apoquel's target column reads 'JAK1 inhibitor' and Librela's
'anti-NGF monoclonal antibody', so neither molecule name was indexed and a human JAK or NGF asset
found no competitor at all. Drug names are therefore indexed too, and 'class:' keys carry the
mechanism a human and a companion-animal asset would actually share.
